---
title: "Temperature"
description: "A decoding parameter that controls how concentrated or varied a model's sampling distribution is."
term: "Temperature"
letter: "T"
category: "LLM Engineering"
difficulty: "Beginner"
---

## Simple explanation

Temperature changes how predictable sampled model outputs tend to be.
Lower values favor the highest-scoring options more strongly; higher values
spread probability more broadly and can produce more varied text.

## Technical explanation

For logits $z_i$ and positive temperature $T$, sampling commonly applies
$\mathrm{softmax}(z_i/T)$. Lowering $T$ sharpens the distribution, while
raising it flattens the distribution. Temperature changes sampling
probabilities, not the underlying model parameters.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Temperature is a simple way to tune the trade-off between repeatability and
variety in generation. Its effect depends on the prompt, model, other
decoding controls, and task, so it should be evaluated rather than treated
as a universal creativity setting.

## How it works

The decoder divides logits by the temperature before normalizing them into
probabilities. The next token is sampled from that distribution. A very
low temperature makes outputs more deterministic but does not guarantee
correctness; a high temperature increases the chance of lower-ranked
tokens.

## Practical example

A structured extraction task may use a low temperature to reduce variation,
while an ideation task may benefit from a higher one. Compare outputs on
fixed prompts and check validity and task quality for each setting.

## Common misconceptions

- Temperature does not add knowledge or improve factual accuracy by itself.
- A temperature of zero is handled differently by providers and may select
  the highest-scoring token rather than perform sampling.
